aimTitle: Develop a website to meet client requirements
aimShort: Common tools and techniques; website development processes; testing
board: Pearson BTEC Level 3 National Extended Certificate in IT (AAQ)

topics.name: Common tools and techniques to produce a website

checklist.name: HTML (HyperText Markup Language): the structure of a webpage. Elements include navigation (menus, internal and external links, anchors), adding content (text, images, video, tables of information), and forms (input fields, textareas, buttons, dropdowns). Semantic HTML uses meaningful tags like <header>, <nav>, <main>, <section>, <footer>, <article> for accessibility and SEO.

CSS (Cascading Style Sheets): the presentation. Styling (colour, web typography, text formatting, links and buttons, tables, forms), page layout (CSS box model — content, padding, border, margin; responsive layouts using CSS media queries and layout tools like Flexbox and Grid)

JavaScript: adds interactivity. Displaying images (sliders, galleries), displaying information (accordions, tabs, modal boxes, filtering information), animation (hover effects, transitions, animated logos, motion), search functionality, shopping carts, interactive maps, video (controlling video playback, video backgrounds)
Web development tools: text editors (VS Code), WYSIWYG editors (Adobe Dreamweaver), browser developer tools, version control (Git)
Development process: plan → design → build → test → review → refine → publish
Accessibility features: alternative text (alt tags) on images, zoom features, text-to-speech
Accessibility standards: WCAG (Web Content Accessibility Guidelines), W3C standards, HTML5 standards
Semantic HTML: using meaningful structural tags improves accessibility for screen readers and SEO
Search Engine Optimisation (SEO): keywords, meta tags (title, description), heading structure, alt text, fast loading, mobile-friendly design, internal links
Self-review: quality in comparison to similar websites, suitability for audience and purpose, meeting client requirements, legal and ethical constraints, consistency, readability
Publishing the website: choosing a hosting provider/domain, uploading files via FTP or a hosting dashboard, testing the live site

Functionality testing: creating a test plan (description, test data, expected outcome, actual outcome, comments), testing areas including links (do all navigation links work?), user interactivity (do buttons, forms, accordions, sliders work?), and responsiveness (does it work at different screen sizes?)

Usability testing: a user testing audit with real users — asking classmates/friends/family to try the site and give feedback; testing areas include accessibility, logical navigation, clarity of information, user experience
Refinements: use the outcomes of testing and self-review to make improvements to the final website

mcq.q: Which HTML element is semantic (has meaning for accessibility and SEO)?
mcq.why: Semantic elements like <header>, <nav>, <main>, <section> and <footer> describe their meaning, helping screen readers and search engines.

mcq.q: Which describes the CSS box model?
mcq.why: Every element is a box: content in the middle, then padding (space inside), border, and margin (space outside).

mcq.q: How do you make a layout responsive to different screen sizes?
options: Media queries and responsive layout tools like Flexbox and Grid
mcq.why: Media queries apply different styles at different screen widths, and Flexbox/Grid layouts flex to fit. Never rely on fixed widths alone.

mcq.q: Which JavaScript-powered component reveals and hides content in a collapsible section?
mcq.why: An accordion lets users expand and collapse sections â€” great for FAQs. Modals overlay the page; carousels slide images.

mcq.q: What does a modal box do?
options: Opens an overlay on top of the page (e.g. an enlarged image or a sign-in dialog)
mcq.why: A modal displays content in an overlay. Clicking a thumbnail to view a larger image in a modal is a common assignment requirement.

mcq.q: Which organisation publishes the WCAG accessibility guidelines?
mcq.why: The World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) publishes the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG).

mcq.q: What is the purpose of alt text on an image?
options: Adds a border around the image
Describes the image for screen readers and shows if the image fails to load
mcq.why: Alt text gives a text description of the image for screen readers and appears when the image can't load.

mcq.q: Which of these would you check during functionality testing?
options: Whether users find the site intuitive
Whether the brand name is memorable
mcq.why: Functionality testing checks that things WORK â€” links, buttons, forms, interactions and responsiveness. Usability testing checks how real users experience the site.

mcq.q: What is usability testing?
options: Running the site through a code validator
Asking real users to try the site and give feedback on navigation, clarity and experience
Checking the site loads on one computer
mcq.why: Usability testing uses real users (classmates, friends, family) to audit the experience â€” accessibility, logical navigation, clarity and overall UX.

mcq.q: What is a test plan?
options: A schedule of when to write code
A table of tests listing description, test data, expected outcome, actual outcome and comments
A wireframe of the final site
mcq.why: A formal test plan documents each test so you can compare expected vs actual outcomes â€” essential evidence for the assignment.

mcq.q: What should your self-review of the finished website consider?
options: Quality vs similar sites, suitability for the audience, meeting client requirements, consistency and readability
mcq.why: The spec's self-review covers comparison with similar websites, audience and purpose suitability, client requirements, legal/ethical constraints, consistency and readability.

mcq.q: Which HTML tag is used to create a hyperlink?
mcq.why: The (anchor) tag creates links using the href attribute, e.g. Link.

mcq.q: Which HTML element is used for a form?
mcq.why: The <form> element wraps form controls like inputs, selects and buttons, and defines how data is submitted.

mcq.q: Which HTML tag embeds a video?
mcq.why: The <video> element embeds video with controls, e.g. <video controls src="clip.mp4"></video>.

mcq.q: What is the purpose of the <nav> element?
options: To mark up a block of navigation links
mcq.why: <nav> is a semantic element that identifies navigation links, helping screen readers and SEO understand the structure.

mcq.q: What does CSS stand for?
mcq.why: CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) controls the presentation â€” layout, colours, fonts and spacing â€” of HTML content.

mcq.q: Which CSS property changes the text colour?
mcq.why: The color property sets text colour; background sets the background; font-size sets size; text-align aligns text.

mcq.q: What is a media query used for?
options: Applying different styles based on screen size or device
mcq.why: Media queries (e.g. @media (max-width: 600px)) apply CSS only under certain conditions â€” the basis of responsive design.

mcq.q: What is Flexbox used for?
options: Laying out elements in a flexible row or column
mcq.why: Flexbox arranges items in one dimension (row or column) and handles spacing, alignment and wrapping â€” great for nav bars and cards.

mcq.q: What is JavaScript used for on a website?
options: Adding interactivity like sliders, forms and dynamic content
mcq.why: JavaScript adds behaviour and interactivity â€” responding to clicks, validating forms, animating and updating content.

mcq.q: What does a carousel/slider do?
options: Cycles through a set of images or slides
mcq.why: A carousel automatically or manually cycles through slides â€” common for galleries, testimonials and featured content.

mcq.q: What is a tab component?
options: A set of buttons that switch between different content panels
mcq.why: Tabs let users switch between sections of content without leaving the page â€” a common interactive component.

mcq.q: What is a filter/search feature?
options: Lets users narrow down a list by typing or selecting criteria
mcq.why: Search/filter functionality lets users find items quickly â€” a common assignment requirement (e.g. filtering a product list).

mcq.q: What is a skip link?
options: A link that lets keyboard users jump straight to the main content
mcq.why: A skip link ('Skip to main content') lets keyboard and screen-reader users bypass repeated navigation â€” an accessibility best practice.

mcq.q: What is semantic HTML?
options: Using elements that describe their meaning (e.g. <header>, <main>)
HTML that only works in one browser
mcq.why: Semantic HTML uses meaningful tags, improving accessibility, SEO and code readability compared to generic <div>s.

mcq.q: Why is the lang attribute important on the <html> element?
options: It tells screen readers and search engines the page language
mcq.why: The lang attribute (e.g. lang="en") helps screen readers pronounce content correctly and helps search engines index the language.

mcq.q: What is a heading hierarchy?
options: Using h1, h2, h3 in a logical order to structure content
mcq.why: A logical heading hierarchy (one h1, then h2/h3 for subsections) helps screen readers and search engines understand structure.

mcq.q: What is a sitemap in the context of SEO?
options: A file listing all pages of a site to help search engines index it
mcq.why: An XML sitemap lists all URLs so search engines can discover and index pages efficiently.

mcq.q: What is a test plan's 'expected outcome'?
options: What the site should do if the feature works correctly
mcq.why: The expected outcome is the correct result you predict; comparing it to the actual outcome reveals whether the feature works.

mcq.q: What is a test plan's 'actual outcome'?
options: What the site actually did when tested
mcq.why: The actual outcome records what really happened, so you can compare it to the expected outcome and note any defects.

mcq.q: What is a defect/bug?
options: An error or fault in the website that stops it working as intended
mcq.why: A defect is any flaw â€” a broken link, a form that won't submit, a layout that breaks on mobile â€” that needs fixing.

mcq.q: Why test a website on a mobile device?
options: To check the responsive layout works and content is usable on small screens
mcq.why: Most users browse on mobile, so you must verify the responsive layout, touch targets and readability on small screens.

mcq.q: What is a usability audit?
options: A structured review of how easy and pleasant the site is to use
mcq.why: A usability audit assesses navigation, clarity, accessibility and overall user experience â€” often with real users.

mcq.q: What is a refinement?
options: A change made to improve the website after testing or review
mcq.why: Refinements are improvements made in response to testing and feedback â€” showing the review cycle is key evidence.

mcq.q: Why document the improvements you made after testing?
options: Because it is required by law
To show the examiner you reviewed and refined your work
mcq.why: Documenting before â†’ feedback â†’ after shows the review cycle, which is essential for higher grades in the assignment.

mcq.q: Which HTML element is used for a table?
mcq.why: The <table> element creates tables, with <tr> for rows, <th> for headers and <td> for cells.

mcq.q: What is the purpose of the CSS 'margin' property?
options: To add space inside an element
To add space outside an element, pushing it away from neighbours
mcq.why: Margin adds space outside the border; padding adds space inside. Both control spacing in the box model.

mcq.q: What is an event listener in JavaScript?
options: Code that waits for an action (like a click) and runs a function in response
mcq.why: Event listeners (e.g. addEventListener('click', ...)) make elements interactive by responding to user actions.

quiz.q: Which HTML tag creates an internal link to another page of the same site?
quiz.why: Internal links use <a> with a relative href to another file in the site (about.html). <link> is for stylesheets.

quiz.q: Which CSS rule makes a website adapt to a small phone screen?
quiz.why: Media queries apply specific styles when the viewport matches, e.g. max-width: 600px for phones.

quiz.q: A tester clicks every nav link and records which work. This is:
quiz.why: Functionality testing verifies features work — links, buttons, forms. Usability testing asks real users about the experience.

quiz.q: Which is an example of publishing a website?
options: Saving files to a USB stick
Uploading files to a web host so they are live on the internet
quiz.why: Publishing means making the site publicly accessible — uploading to hosting (e.g. GitHub Pages, Netlify) with a domain.

flashcards.back: Using meaningful tags (<header>, <nav>, <main>, <article>, <footer>) that describe structure — improves accessibility and SEO.
Every element is a box: content → padding → border → margin. Understanding it is essential for layout and spacing.
A CSS rule (@media) that applies styles based on viewport size — the basis of responsive design.
Collapsible sections that expand and contract (powered by JavaScript) — ideal for FAQs and long content lists.
An overlay dialog on top of the page — commonly used for image lightboxes and sign-in forms.
Alternative text describing an image for screen readers, shown if the image fails to load. Required for accessibility.
Testing that the site works: links, buttons, forms, interactivity and responsiveness. Recorded in a test plan (expected vs actual outcome).
Getting real users (classmates, friends) to try the site and give feedback on navigation, clarity, accessibility and experience.
Reflecting on the finished site: quality vs similar sites, suitability for audience/purpose, meeting client requirements, consistency and readability — then refining.
Legal protection for created work (images, text, music, video). Using others' work without permission breaches the Copyright, Designs and Patents Act.
Data protection law covering personal data collected by websites — privacy policy, consent, only collecting what you need, safe form handling.

criteria.text: Use tools, techniques, processes and testing to produce a website that partially meets the client's requirements.
Use tools, techniques, processes and testing to produce a website that meets most of the client's requirements.
Use tools, techniques, processes and testing to produce a website that comprehensively meets the client's requirements.

briefs.title: Retro Film Hub
briefs.scenario: Midnight Picture Show is a small independent cinema that hosts late-night screenings of classic films. They want a website that introduces young adults (17-23) to the films, stars and cultural moments of Hollywood's golden era.
briefs.purpose: To introduce a young adult audience to classic films and encourage them to visit the cinema.
briefs.targetAudience: 17- to 23-year-olds — many will have seen remakes or references to old films but never the originals.
mustIncludes: Three pages
Drop-down menus
Information about classic films (plot summaries, iconic stars, behind-the-scenes facts)
An accordion (e.g. 'Explore by genre or decade' with expandable sections)
External links to relevant websites (e.g. film archive sites, the cinema's ticketing site)
A form to request a specific film be screened
Modal images (click a film poster to view it enlarged)
Video content with controls (trailers — always embed from official sources)
Search functionality to find films
Accessibility features (alt text, high contrast, keyboard navigation, readable fonts)
briefs.typographyHint: Try a bold display font for headings to echo old cinema signage, with a clean sans-serif for body text.
briefs.colourHint: Golden-era Hollywood palette: deep burgundy, cream, gold and black — or teal and burnt orange for a vintage poster feel.

briefs.title: Community Action Charity
briefs.scenario: A non-profit organisation wants a website to create awareness of its activities and encourage teenagers to join as volunteers. It needs to show positive representations of its members and its work in the community.
briefs.purpose: To create awareness of the charity and encourage a teenage audience to get involved.
mustIncludes: Three pages
Information about the organisation (aims, activities, achievements)
Information about an upcoming event, including a map of the location
One member's personal story (with permission)
An email link to contact the organisation
A form to join the organisation
An interactive image slider with captions
A resource section with filter functionality (text, infographics and video resources)
Positive representations of the organisation and its members
Accessibility features
briefs.typographyHint: Friendly, rounded fonts for headings; clean body text. Avoid jargon — write for teenagers.
briefs.colourHint: Bright, energetic palette (e.g. teal, coral, sunshine yellow) with strong contrast for accessibility.

briefs.title: Local Sports & Fitness Club
briefs.scenario: A local multi-sport club wants a website that promotes its teams and fitness sessions. The club wants to grow its membership among 16-25 year olds and needs the site to showcase facilities, timetables and how to join.
briefs.purpose: To promote the club's teams, sessions and facilities and convert visitors into members.
briefs.targetAudience: 16- to 25-year-olds, including students new to the area
mustIncludes: Three pages
Drop-down menus (sports, sessions, membership)
Information about sports and fitness sessions
An accordion (e.g. frequently asked questions)
External links (e.g. national sport governing bodies)
A form to register interest in joining
Modal images (photo gallery with lightbox)
Video content with controls (session highlights)
Search functionality
Accessibility features
briefs.typographyHint: Strong condensed headings for a sporty energy; keep body text highly readable.
briefs.colourHint: High-contrast sport palette (e.g. royal blue and volt/highlighter accents) — check contrast ratios pass WCAG.

notes.title: Development & testing

A [[test plan]] lists each test with its expected [[outcome]], actual [[result]], and any [[actions]] needed.

designs.title: Form design
designs.prompt: Design the "request a screening" form for the cinema site. Show fields, suitable input types, validation and a clear submit button.

designs.title: Website test plan
designs.prompt: Write a test plan for the built cinema site: test, expected outcome, actual result and any fix. Cover functionality, usability and accessibility.

designs.title: Client review report
designs.prompt: Sketch the layout of a review report for the cinema client, summarising what was built and how it meets the brief.

scenario.text: Midnight Picture Show is a small independent cinema that hosts late-night screenings of classic films. It wants a website that introduces young adults (17–23) to the films, stars and cultural moments of Hollywood's golden era and encourages them to book tickets.
scenario.audience: Target audience: 17- to 23-year-olds, many of whom have seen remakes or references but never the originals.

tasks.name: Research & plan the website
steps: Read the brief and highlight the purpose, audience and must-include features.
Research 2–3 existing websites and compare what they do well / badly.
Produce a site map showing every page and how they link.
tasks.distinction: Use pertinent, named examples and a clearly annotated site map showing HOW each page meets the brief. Use accurate technical vocabulary (SEO, accessibility, UX).

tasks.name: Design the website & manage assets
steps: Sketch wireframes for every page, then a high-fidelity visual design.
Source or create assets and keep an asset log with licences.
Review your designs against the brief and refine them.
tasks.distinction: Justify every design choice against the audience and brief. Show a clear link between wireframe, mockup and final site, with effective asset management.

tasks.name: Build, test & review the website
steps: Build the site to your design using the required tools and techniques.
Test functionality, usability and accessibility; log results and fixes.
Write a self-review of strengths, weaknesses and improvements.
tasks.distinction: Demonstrate web standards, a consistent and accessible site, effective testing, and considered refinements drawn from a thorough self-review.
